ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Consider a rectangular loop made of superconducting material with length $\ell=200 \mathrm{~cm}$ and width $w=2 \mathrm{~cm}$. The radius of this particular wire is $r=0.5 \mathrm{~mm}$. This superconducting rectangular loop initially has a current $I_{1}=5 \mathrm{~A}$ in the counterclockwise direction as shown in the figure below. This rectangular loop is situated a distance $d=1 \mathrm{~cm}$ above an infinitely long wire that initially contains no current. Suppose that the current in the infinitely long wire is increased to some current $I_{2}$ such that there is an attractive force $F$ between the rectangular loop and the long wire. Find the maximum possible value of $F$. Write your answer in newtons.
Hint: You may neglect the magnetic field produced by the vertical segments in the rectangular loop.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a rectangular superconducting loop located above an infinitely long horizontal straight wire. The distance from the lower side of the rectangle to the long straight wire is labeled d, the vertical height of the rectangle is labeled w, and the horizontal length is labeled ℓ. In the figure, the loop current I1 is in the counterclockwise direction: the current on the lower side is to the right, the current on the upper side is to the left, the left side is downward, and the right side is upward. Reasoning: In order to make there be an attractive force between the long straight wire and the rectangular loop, take the long straight wire current I2 to the right. In this way the lower side of the rectangular loop is in the same direction as the long straight wire and attracts, and the upper side is opposite to the long straight wire and repels, but the upper side is farther away, so the net force can be attractive. The magnetic flux of the superconducting loop is conserved. Initially the long straight wire current is 0, and the loop current is I1, so the conservation relation is L I1. After adding the long straight wire current I2, the loop current becomes I, and there is L I + M I2 = L I1, so I = I1 - (M/L) I2. According to the problem's hint, ignoring the contribution of the vertical sides, the mutual inductance is M = (μ0 ℓ / 2π) ln((d+w)/d), and the loop self-inductance is approximately L ≈ (μ0 ℓ / π) ln(w/r). The magnitude of the net force between the two horizontal sides and the long straight wire is F = (μ0 ℓ I I2 / 2π) [1/d - 1/(d+w)]. Substituting I = I1 - (M/L)I2 gives F = A[I1 I2 - (M/L)I2^2], where A = (μ0 ℓ / 2π)[1/d - 1/(d+w)]. This is a quadratic function of I2 opening downward, and the maximum value appears at I2 = L I1/(2M). At this time Fmax = A L I1^2/(4M). Substituting numerical values: ℓ=2 m, w=0.02 m, d=0.01 m, r=5.0×10^-4 m, I1=5 A. ln(w/r)=ln(40), ln((d+w)/d)=ln(3). Therefore L/M = 2 ln(40)/ln(3) ≈ 6.716, A = (4π×10^-7 × 2 / 2π)(100 - 33.333...) ≈ 2.667×10^-5. So Fmax = 2.667×10^-5 × (6.716)(25/4) ≈ 1.12×10^-3 N.

raw_record.question_text:
Consider a rectangular loop made of superconducting material with length $\ell=200 \mathrm{~cm}$ and width $w=2 \mathrm{~cm}$. The radius of this particular wire is $r=0.5 \mathrm{~mm}$. This superconducting rectangular loop initially has a current $I_{1}=5 \mathrm{~A}$ in the counterclockwise direction as shown in the figure below. This rectangular loop is situated a distance $d=1 \mathrm{~cm}$ above an infinitely long wire that initially contains no current. Suppose that the current in the infinitely long wire is increased to some current $I_{2}$ such that there is an attractive force $F$ between the rectangular loop and the long wire. Find the maximum possible value of $F$. Write your answer in newtons.
Hint: You may neglect the magnetic field produced by the vertical segments in the rectangular loop.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a long straight wire below a rectangular superconducting loop: the lower horizontal segment of the loop is distance d above the long wire, the upper segment is distance d+w above it, both horizontal segments have length ℓ, and the indicated loop current is counterclockwise so the lower segment current points right while the upper segment points left. For attraction, take I2 in the long wire to the right so the lower segment is attracted downward and the farther upper segment is repelled upward. Use superconducting flux conservation: initially the long wire has no current, so the conserved flux linkage is L I1. After I2 is applied, L I + M I2 = L I1, where I is the new loop current, M = (μ0 ℓ / 2π) ln((d+w)/d), and, neglecting vertical sides, L ≈ (μ0 ℓ / π) ln(w/r). The force magnitude from the two horizontal segments is F = (μ0 ℓ I I2 / 2π)(1/d - 1/(d+w)). Substitute I = I1 - (M/L)I2 to get a concave quadratic in I2. Maximize it at I2 = L I1/(2M), giving Fmax = [(μ0 ℓ)/(2π)(1/d - 1/(d+w))] L I1^2/(4M). Insert ℓ=2 m, w=0.02 m, d=0.01 m, r=5e-4 m, I1=5 A to obtain about 1.12e-3 N.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中有一个长方形 superconducting loop 位于一根无限长水平直导线的上方。长方形下边离长直导线的距离标为 d，长方形竖直高度标为 w，水平长度标为 ℓ。图中环路电流 I1 为逆时针方向：下边电流向右，上边电流向左，左边向下，右边向上。

推理：为了使长直导线和矩形环之间有吸引力，取长直导线电流 I2 向右。这样矩形环下边与长直导线同向而相吸，上边与长直导线反向而相斥，但上边距离更远，所以净力可以为吸引。

超导回路磁通守恒。初始长直导线电流为 0，回路电流为 I1，因此守恒关系为 L I1。加上长直导线电流 I2 后，回路电流变为 I，有
L I + M I2 = L I1,
所以
I = I1 - (M/L) I2。

按题目提示忽略竖直边贡献，互感为
M = (μ0 ℓ / 2π) ln((d+w)/d)，
回路自感近似为
L ≈ (μ0 ℓ / π) ln(w/r)。

水平两边与长直导线的净力大小为
F = (μ0 ℓ I I2 / 2π) [1/d - 1/(d+w)]。
代入 I = I1 - (M/L)I2，得到
F = A[I1 I2 - (M/L)I2^2],
其中
A = (μ0 ℓ / 2π)[1/d - 1/(d+w)]。
这是关于 I2 的开口向下二次函数，最大值出现在
I2 = L I1/(2M)。
此时
Fmax = A L I1^2/(4M)。

代入数值：ℓ=2 m，w=0.02 m，d=0.01 m，r=5.0×10^-4 m，I1=5 A。
ln(w/r)=ln(40)，ln((d+w)/d)=ln(3)。
因此
L/M = 2 ln(40)/ln(3) ≈ 6.716，
A = (4π×10^-7 × 2 / 2π)(100 - 33.333...) ≈ 2.667×10^-5。
所以
Fmax = 2.667×10^-5 × (6.716)(25/4) ≈ 1.12×10^-3 N。

method.method_draft: Use the same visual geometry but formulate the force through inductance/virtual work. From the diagram, let x be the separation between the long wire and the lower horizontal side of the loop; the upper side is at x+w and the horizontal span is ℓ. The mutual inductance of the long wire with the loop is M(x) = (μ0 ℓ / 2π) ln((x+w)/x). The downward attractive force magnitude can be obtained from the mutual-inductance gradient: F = I I2[-dM/dx] evaluated at x=d, so -M'(d) = (μ0 ℓ / 2π)(1/d - 1/(d+w)). Superconducting flux linkage conservation gives L I + M(d) I2 = L I1, with L ≈ (μ0 ℓ / π)ln(w/r). Instead of optimizing over I2, solve I2 = (L/M)(I1 - I), so F = [-M'(d)](L/M) I(I1-I). This product is maximized when I = I1/2, by symmetry or AM-GM, yielding the same Fmax = [-M'(d)] L I1^2/(4M). Substituting the given dimensions and current gives 1.12e-3 N.
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：附图中，一个矩形闭合回路位于一条水平无限长直导线的上方；矩形的水平长度标为 ℓ，竖直宽度标为 w，矩形下边到长直导线的竖直距离标为 d。回路电流箭头沿下边向右、右边向上、上边向左、左边向下，因此是逆时针方向；长直导线在矩形下方水平延伸。推理：令 x 为长直导线到矩形下水平边的距离，则上水平边距离为 x+w。按指定的互感方法，长直导线与矩形回路的互感为 M(x)=(μ0ℓ/2π)ln((x+w)/x)。因此在 x=d 处，-M'(d)=(μ0ℓ/2π)(1/d-1/(d+w))。忽略竖直边贡献时，吸引力大小为 F=I I2[-M'(d)]。超导回路保持磁通链守恒：L I+M(d)I2=L I1，其中 L≈(μ0ℓ/π)ln(w/r)。由此 I2=(L/M)(I1-I)，所以 F=[-M'(d)](L/M)I(I1-I)。该二次式在 I=I1/2 时最大，因此 Fmax=[-M'(d)]L I1^2/(4M)。代入 ℓ=2.00 m，w=0.020 m，d=0.010 m，r=5.0×10^-4 m，I1=5 A：M=(μ0ℓ/2π)ln3=4.394×10^-7 H，-M'(d)=(μ0ℓ/2π)(100-33.333)=2.667×10^-5 H/m，L=(μ0ℓ/π)ln40=2.951×10^-6 H。于是 Fmax=(2.667×10^-5)(2.951×10^-6)(25)/(4×4.394×10^-7)=1.12×10^-3 N。

raw_record.original_question:
Consider a rectangular loop made of superconducting material with length $\ell=200 \mathrm{~cm}$ and width $w=2 \mathrm{~cm}$. The radius of this particular wire is $r=0.5 \mathrm{~mm}$. This superconducting rectangular loop initially has a current $I_{1}=5 \mathrm{~A}$ in the counterclockwise direction as shown in the figure below. This rectangular loop is situated a distance $d=1 \mathrm{~cm}$ above an infinitely long wire that initially contains no current. Suppose that the current in the infinitely long wire is increased to some current $I_{2}$ such that there is an attractive force $F$ between the rectangular loop and the long wire. Find the maximum possible value of $F$. Write your answer in newtons.
Hint: You may neglect the magnetic field produced by the vertical segments in the rectangular loop.
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure there is a rectangular superconducting loop located above an infinitely long horizontal straight wire. The distance from the lower side of the rectangle to the long straight wire is labeled d, the vertical height of the rectangle is labeled w, and the horizontal length is labeled ℓ. In the figure, the loop current I1 is in the counterclockwise direction: the current on the lower side is to the right, the current on the upper side is to the left, the left side is downward, and the right side is upward.

Reasoning: In order to make there be an attractive force between the long straight wire and the rectangular loop, take the long straight wire current I2 to the right. In this way the lower side of the rectangular loop is in the same direction as the long straight wire and attracts, and the upper side is opposite to the long straight wire and repels, but the upper side is farther away, so the net force can be attractive.

The magnetic flux of the superconducting loop is conserved. Initially the long straight wire current is 0, and the loop current is I1, so the conservation relation is L I1. After adding the long straight wire current I2, the loop current becomes I, and there is
L I + M I2 = L I1,
so
I = I1 - (M/L) I2.

According to the problem's hint, ignoring the contribution of the vertical sides, the mutual inductance is
M = (μ0 ℓ / 2π) ln((d+w)/d),
and the loop self-inductance is approximately
L ≈ (μ0 ℓ / π) ln(w/r).

The magnitude of the net force between the two horizontal sides and the long straight wire is
F = (μ0 ℓ I I2 / 2π) [1/d - 1/(d+w)].
Substituting I = I1 - (M/L)I2 gives
F = A[I1 I2 - (M/L)I2^2],
where
A = (μ0 ℓ / 2π)[1/d - 1/(d+w)].
This is a quadratic function of I2 opening downward, and the maximum value appears at
I2 = L I1/(2M).
At this time
Fmax = A L I1^2/(4M).

Substituting numerical values: ℓ=2 m, w=0.02 m, d=0.01 m, r=5.0×10^-4 m, I1=5 A.
ln(w/r)=ln(40), ln((d+w)/d)=ln(3).
Therefore
L/M = 2 ln(40)/ln(3) ≈ 6.716,
A = (4π×10^-7 × 2 / 2π)(100 - 33.333...) ≈ 2.667×10^-5.
So
Fmax = 2.667×10^-5 × (6.716)(25/4) ≈ 1.12×10^-3 N.
